subject: chemistry-2
question: Using a 5 M stock solution, a technician needs to prepare 250 mL of a 0.4 M working solution for a teaching laboratory. What volume of stock solution should be measured out, and how should it be handled afterward?

options.text: 50 mL of stock, then add solvent until the total volume reaches 250 mL
20 mL of stock, then add solvent until the total volume reaches 250 mL
20 mL of stock, then add exactly 250 mL of solvent to that portion
125 mL of stock, then add solvent until the total volume reaches 250 mL

explanation:
Rearranging M1V1 = M2V2 gives V1 = (0.4 M x 250 mL) / 5 M = 20 mL of stock. That aliquot is then brought up to a final total volume of 250 mL rather than having 250 mL of solvent added to it, which would produce 270 mL and a concentration of about 0.37 M. Distinguishing dilute to a final volume from add this volume of solvent is a core laboratory technique point, and it is why volumetric flasks are filled to a calibration mark.

ELI-10: Work from the solute the final solution must contain: 0.4 mol/L x 0.25 L = 0.1 mol. The stock carries 5 mol in every liter, so 0.1 mol occupies 0.1/5 = 0.02 L, which is 20 mL. Transfer that 20 mL to the flask and add solvent until the meniscus reaches the 250 mL mark. Filling to a mark is not the same instruction as adding 250 mL, since the second approach overshoots the target volume and leaves the solution slightly too dilute.
source: OpenStax — Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e); NIST — Reference Data / Constants (https://www.nist.gov/pml)
